system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: the interpreter constructs a detailed prompt with four elements
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt = Task Description + Current Progress + Observation + Current Instruction, rendered per step.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Task Description: The query that defines the entire program, acting as the primary input to guide the system's operations.
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/environment context injection described; tools are domain APIs.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: we store a large volume of intermediate results in temporary memory, retrieving relevant information as needed in subsequent steps
context_compaction.note: Observations are selectively retrieved rather than all included; closest value.

observation_format.evidence_quote: the observation represents the results of tool execution, such as search results

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Call a tool? Tool name? Arguments?
tool_call_format.note: Tool name and args are extracted from LLM free-text output by the interpreter; not a provider tool-call API.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: the system will select the suitable tool, configure it with the necessary parameters, execute it, and integrate the output into the ongoing process
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive described; tools are search/model APIs.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Select models in provided models list to generate a to-do list.
tool_schema_source.note: Tool/model list supplied in prompt; no schema generator described.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: we equip the designed interpreter with the capability to invoke external tools
protocol_standardization.note: No protocol (MCP/A2A) mentioned in the CoRE paper; AIOS README mentions MCP server for computer-use, separate system.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the system executes a single step in four procedures
loop_primitives.note: Default: execution of a human-written flow program (fixed_pipeline with branching); each step includes observe/act like react.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Step Connection: Step connections define the progression from one step to another, establishing the flow of the program execution.
planning_granularity.note: The CoRE program itself is an explicit, stored step graph, authored by a human.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: CoRE, which takes LLM as the interpreter to interpret and execute the instructions in natural language

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: utilizes a Large Language Model (LLM) as an interpreter to execute programs written in the CoRE language

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: it currently relies on manually crafted programs
human_in_loop.note: Human authors the program up front; no in-run gating described.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Current Progress: Summarizes the previous steps including what has been done or decided, helping maintain a narrative flow.
short_term_state.note: State = current step pointer + progress + memory of observations, not a raw message list.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The system's memory serves as a repository of all prior observations related to the program
long_term_memory.note: Memory is within-run only; no cross-run persistence described.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: we store a large volume of intermediate results in temporary memory

self_verification.evidence_quote: demanding the LLM interpreter to evaluate the current results so as to identify the most suitable subsequent step
self_verification.note: Branch evaluation is control flow, not a verification mechanism; no harness-run tests/linters/judge.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Terminal steps, by definition, do not lead to any future steps, indicating the end of program execution.
retry_policy.note: Loops are program-level iteration, not task-level retry.

rollback.evidence_quote: Finally, after executing the current step, the interpreter will determine the next step based on step type and execution results.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Terminal: Similar to the "end" or "return" statement, this step marks the conclusion of the program
termination_condition.note: Termination when the program flow reaches a Terminal step.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Considering the LLM's limitation on the number of input tokens (context window size), including all runtime information in the input prompt is impractical.
cost_controls.note: Context is reduced by selective retrieval, but no budget/caching/routing mechanism is described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Specifically, if tool usage is warranted, the system will select the suitable tool, configure it with the necessary parameters, execute it
timeouts.note: No timeout described at the point tools are executed.

network_policy.evidence_quote: they often fall short in tasks that require domain-specific knowledge or up-to-date information
network_policy.note: External search tools imply unrestricted network; no policy described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: the interpreter will make a decision about if or not to employ specialized tools based on the LLM's initial response

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We conduct experiments on a benchmark dataset, OpenAGI
eval_hooks.note: Benchmark lives in the separate OpenAGI platform repo.

guardrails.evidence_quote: if tool usage is warranted, the system will select the suitable tool, configure it with the necessary parameters, execute it, and integrate the output into the ongoing process
guardrails.note: No pre-execution validation or filtering described.

target_domain.evidence_quote: we equip the designed interpreter with the capability to invoke external tools, compensating for the limitations of LLM in specialized domains
target_domain.note: Agent programming / tool orchestration, not repository SWE.

open_source.evidence_quote: This work is open-source at https://github.com/agiresearch/CoRE
open_source.note: Licence file not inspected; AIOS repo ships LICENSE.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We conduct experiments on both closed-source and open-source LLMs
model_agnostic.note: GPT-4 and Mixtral both used as interpreters.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: AIOS Compiler: LLM as Interpreter for Natural Language Programming and Flow Programming of AI Agents
primary_artifact.note: Only the paper is available as evidence here; the CoRE repo itself was not supplied, pinned evidence is the AIOS repo.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv v1 date implied by the 2405.06907 identifier; no tag evidence available.

pinned_version.note: CoRE's own repo was not supplied; pinned reference is the AIOS kernel repo plus paper arXiv:2405.06907v2.

stars.note: Stars of agiresearch/AIOS, not the CoRE repo.
